hits.heading: No automatic transaction retries
hits.body: Checkout does not automatically retry inventory or payment transactions. The investigator's tools only read observations and reviewed guidance. Suggested verification steps must not become automatic restarts, configuration changes, repeated charges, or shell execution.

hits.heading: Verification and limits
hits.body: Read-only verification compares both sides of the request with the applicable service map. hits.heading: Bounded requests
hits.body: Checkout configures a one-second HTTP client timeout for dependency calls and does not retry transactions automatically. hits.heading: Response failure versus transport failure
hits.body: A downstream request failed record with an HTTP status means an error response was received. A downstream request unavailable record without a status indicates a transport problem such as timeout, name resolution failure, or refused connection. This generic message does not distinguish those causes. Do not claim an unmeasured timeout duration.

hits.heading: Observed recovery
hits.body: A later business request returning HTTP 200 demonstrates recovery for that request at that time. It does not prove service health during an earlier incident or reveal why the earlier request failed. Avoid extending one observation into a continuous availability claim.

hits.body: Checkout configures a one-second HTTP client timeout for dependency calls and does not retry transactions automatically. Compare recorded duration, neighboring requests, and downstream logs. The configured timeout does not prove that every unavailable response was a timeout. Timeout categories apply to phases of the HTTP operation rather than guaranteeing a one-second total duration.

hits.title: Dependency timeouts and network reachability
hits.heading: Response failure versus transport failure
hits.body: A downstream request failed record with an HTTP status means an error response was received. A downstream request unavailable record without a status indicates a transport problem such as timeout, name resolution failure, or refused connection. This generic message does not distinguish those causes. Do not claim an unmeasured timeout duration.

hits.title: Process liveness versus business availability
hits.heading: Observed recovery
hits.body: A later business request returning HTTP 200 demonstrates recovery for that request at that time. It does not prove service health during an earlier incident or reveal why the earlier request failed. Avoid extending one observation into a continuous availability claim.

limitations: Runbooks are guidance, not observations or proof of a root cause.
Cosine filtering is a heuristic, not calibrated relevance confidence.
